text:
Predicates:
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
Backbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
QueenBee(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Harry ::: Harry.

Premises:
Animals(x) → (Invertebrate(x) ∨ Vertebrate(x)) ::: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates.
Vertebrate(x) → Backbone(x) ::: All vertebrate animals have a backbone.
∀x (Backbone(x) ∧ Vertebrate(x)) → ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x) ::: All animals with backbones that are vertebrates reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Bee(x) ∧ ¬ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x)) ::: All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating.
QueenBee(x) → Bee(x) ::: All queen bees are bees.
Harry ::: Harry.

Conclusion:
((Vertebrate(Harry) ∧ Backbone(Harry)) ∨ (¬Vertebrate(Harry) ∧ ¬Backbone(Harry))) → (¬Invertebrate(Harry) ∧ ¬QueenBee(Harry))
